subtopics.title: The Three Weather Systems in One Sweep

questions.question: Which condition is essential for a tropical cyclone but NOT for a mid-latitude cyclone?
options: The Coriolis force
Sea-surface temperatures above about 26,5 degrees Celsius
Low pressure at the centre
Rising air

questions.question: A tropical cyclone cannot form on the equator because:
options: The ocean there is too cold
There is too much land at the equator
The Coriolis force is zero there, so the system cannot gain spin
The trade winds blow too strongly

questions.question: On a synoptic chart, the quickest test that a low south of the country is a mid-latitude cyclone rather than a tropical cyclone is:
options: Fronts attached to the low
Widely spaced isobars
A letter H at its centre
Its position over land

questions.question: A tropical storm is upgraded to a tropical cyclone and receives its name at which point in its development?
options: It is named at the tropical disturbance stage
It is named at the tropical storm stage, before becoming a full tropical cyclone
It is only named once it makes landfall
It is named when the eye disappears

subtopics.title: Anticyclones, Travelling Disturbances and Local Climates

questions.question: Johannesburg's winters are dry and cloudless mainly because:
options: The Kalahari High settles over the plateau with a strong inversion layer capping the interior
Cold fronts never reach the interior
The moisture front strengthens in winter
The urban heat island blocks rainfall

questions.question: A berg wind is hot and dry because the air:
options: Comes from the Mozambique Channel
Passes over the warm Agulhas current
Is heated by veld fires
Sinks from the plateau to the coast and warms by compression

questions.question: On a calm winter night, the warmest zone in a valley is:
options: The valley floor
The thermal belt partway up the slope
The crest of the ridge
The riverbank

questions.question: Which strategy reduces the urban heat island effect?
options: More tarred parking lots in the CBD
Green roofs, parks and tree planting in the city
Removing all wind corridors
Increasing private car use

questions.question: The Orange River rises in the wet Drakensberg and flows through the arid west to the Atlantic. It is best classified as:
options: An episodic river
A periodic river
A permanent and exotic river
A misfit stream

questions.question: A trellis drainage pattern, with tributaries joining at right angles, develops on:
options: Uniform rock with no structural control
Folded landscapes of alternating hard and soft rock layers
A volcanic dome
A flat inland pan

questions.question: Drainage density increases when:
options: Rainfall is low and infiltration is high
Vegetation cover is dense
The rock is highly permeable
Rock is impermeable, slopes are steep and vegetation is sparse

questions.question: A graded river is one that:
options: Has just enough energy to transport its load, with a smooth concave longitudinal profile
Flows only in the wet season
Has many waterfalls and knickpoints
Has been captured by a stronger neighbour

subtopics.title: Fluvial Landforms, Rejuvenation and Catchment Management

questions.question: On a meander, the fastest water and active erosion are found on:
options: The inner slip-off slope
The outer, undercut bank of the bend
The centre of the channel only
The floodplain

questions.question: Which set of features is evidence of river rejuvenation?
options: Delta, levee and braided stream
Elbow of capture, wind gap and misfit stream
Knickpoint, paired terraces and incised meanders
Oxbow lake, slip-off slope and floodplain

questions.question: After river capture, the captured stream typically becomes:
options: A misfit stream, too small for the valley it flows in
A braided stream
An exotic river
A first-order stream

questions.question: Eutrophication in a dam such as Hartbeespoort is caused by:
options: Removal of alien vegetation from the catchment
Nutrient enrichment from sewage and fertiliser run-off feeding algal blooms
Cold water entering from mountain streams
Building fish ladders

questions.question: In the three-characters picture, the quiet giant that sits and squashes stands for:
options: The anticyclone, with sinking, warming, drying air
The mid-latitude cyclone
The tropical cyclone
The coastal low

questions.question: The summer bully from the warm sea starves and weakens when it:
options: Reaches the middle of the warm ocean
Moves over land or cold water and loses its warm-water fuel
Meets the polar front
Crosses the equator

questions.question: The hair-dryer wind that raises fire danger on the coast is:
options: The anabatic valley breeze
The south-westerly behind a cold front
The berg wind, plateau air sinking and warming on its way to the coast
The trade wind

subtopics.title: A River's Whole Life in One Walk

questions.question: The toddler stage of the river — furious, cutting straight down — matches which valley shape?
options: A broad floodplain
A steep V-shaped valley with waterfalls and rapids
A delta
An oxbow lake

questions.question: An oxbow lake is best described as:
options: A lake formed by glacial erosion
A dam built across a meander
The river's source in the mountains
An abandoned meander bend, cut off when the river broke through the neck in flood

questions.question: A gorge that wriggles like a meander — an incised meander — is evidence that:
options: An old, wandering river was rejuvenated and cut its curves down into rock
The river was always young
A delta once existed there
The valley was carved by wind

questions.question: The wind gap left after river capture is:
options: The point where two rivers meet
The dry notch in the ridge where the beheaded river once flowed
The steep outer bank of a meander
A gap in the natural levee

subtopics.title: The Marks You Can Bank Tonight

questions.question: The eight-mark paragraph question in Paper 1 is marked as:
options: Eight bullet points at one mark each
Four ideas at two marks each, written in full sentences
Two ideas at four marks each, in point form
One extended definition

questions.question: Around a low-pressure cell in the Southern Hemisphere, air circulates:
options: Anticlockwise
Straight inward
Clockwise
Clockwise in summer only

questions.question: Why should each drainage pattern be revised together with a rock clue, like trellis with folded layers?
options: Because examiners ask for the pattern together with the underlying rock structure that causes it
Because the pattern names change every year
Because rock types score no marks alone
Because patterns are only visible on orthophoto maps
